h: Getting the Most Out of a Mucky Day
p: Here's the thing about Diggerland: it's at its best when you stop worrying about staying clean. Mud happens. Dust happens. A splash of something brown on your jeans is basically a souvenir. So pack a spare set of clothes for the kids (and maybe for yourself), chuck an old towel in the boot for the seats, and bring a carrier bag for anything that comes home filthy. Your car will thank you on the drive back down the M5.

Timing makes a big difference too. Arriving near the start of the day gives you the best crack at the popular machines before the queues build, and it means you're not rushing the last few rides as the park winds down. School holidays and sunny weekends are naturally the busiest, so if you can manage a term-time visit with younger children, you'll usually get more goes for your effort.

Keep an eye on the forecast as well. Devon can switch from glorious sunshine to sideways drizzle in an afternoon, so sun cream and a waterproof can easily end up in the same bag. Sturdy trainers or wellies beat sandals every time.

If you've still got energy after the diggers, Cullompton sits in a lovely bit of mid Devon. Killerton, the National Trust house and gardens near Broadclyst, is a gentle contrast to all that engine noise, while Tiverton and the Grand Western Canal are handy for a peaceful towpath stroll. A cream tea somewhere along the way? Now you're talking. It rounds off a day of shifting earth beautifully, and the kids will be asleep before you've even hit the motorway.
